They were called Pateras because they were known for their hospitality and generosity towards travelers, particularly pilgrims on their way to the Holy Land. They provided shelter, food, and protection to those in need, and their hospitality became a symbol of the Christian love and compassion.

They were known as Pateras because they were considered spiritual fathers to their communities and provided guidance and support to their followers.
